terms.definition: A rigid outer layer made of cellulose that surrounds the cell membrane and gives a plant cell its fixed, boxy shape.
A thin, flexible layer just inside the cell wall that controls what enters and leaves the cell.
The jelly-like fluid that fills the inside of the cell, where the organelles sit and chemical reactions happen.
The organelle that stores the cell's DNA and directs everything the cell does.
The coded instructions, stored in the nucleus, that tell a cell how to grow, work, and build proteins.
The organelle that breaks down sugar to release energy the cell can use (plural: mitochondria).
A tiny structure that builds proteins by reading instructions copied from DNA.
A folded network of membranes that helps build and move proteins and fats through the cell.
The organelle that packages and ships proteins and other molecules to where they're needed, like a cell's post office.
A large, fluid-filled sac that stores water, nutrients, and waste, and helps keep the cell firm.
The organelle that captures sunlight and uses it to make sugar through photosynthesis.
A network of protein fibers inside the cell that gives it internal structure and helps move materials around.
The process plants use to turn sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide into sugar and oxygen.
The pressure of water pushing the cell membrane against the cell wall, which keeps the cell firm.
